text_blocks.snippet: The most common symptom of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is increasing shortness of breath, especially during physical activities like climbing stairs or exercising.
In the early stages, PAH may cause mild signs that mimic other common heart or lung conditions:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea) during routine tasks

text_blocks.snippet: As the condition progresses and puts more strain on the right side of the heart, more noticeable signs develop: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC (.gov) +2

list.snippet: Swelling (edema) in the ankles, feet, legs, and eventually the abdomen
Heart palpitations (a racing or pounding heartbeat)
Bluish color of the lips and skin (cyanosis)

text_blocks.snippet: If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, would you like to share which specific symptoms are occurring, or if a doctor has already evaluated them?
